correction.question: What happens when I print JSON into a buffer I allocated myself and the output turns out to be bigger than that buffer?
correction.qnorm: what happens when i print json into a buffer i allocated myself and the output turns out to be bigger than that buffer
correction.status_reason: the code at cJSON.c:513 changed or was removed

answer.answer: This is handled in print_preallocated() (test.c:75): it checks `!cJSON_PrintPreallocated(root, buf, (int)len, 1)`, and when that is true it checks `strcmp(out, buf) != 0` (line 77); if true it calls printf(); then it calls free(out) (line 82); then it calls free(buf_fail) (line 83); then it calls free(buf) (line 84); then it returns `-1` (line 85), so the rest of print_preallocated() is skipped. Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: cJSON_PrintPreallocated(), free() — the previous values stay in place.
